name: Stake.com (Medium Rare N.V.) — crypto casino + sportsbook, with a prediction-markets subcategory ("Politics & Entertainment" outrights) inside the sportsbook
positioning: Self-declared hero copy: "The World's Largest Online Casino and Sportsbook." Crypto-native (BTC/ETH/USDT/SOL/TRX + local fiat like CAD/TRY/VND/INR), Curaçao-licensed (OGL/2024/1451/0918), operating since 2017, claiming "over 100 million monthly players" and "over 100,000 bets placed daily." Positioning rests on three pillars: (1) scale/social proof — live player counts, live bet feeds, sponsorships (UFC, Drake, F1 exposure via Kick); (2) a rakeback/VIP economy instead of conventional signup bonuses — no headline deposit-match on the homepage, the whole loyalty story is the VIP Club; (3) in-house content moats — "Stake Originals" provably-fair games and "Only on Stake" exclusives built on Stake Engine. Prediction markets are a leaf node (politics/entertainment outrights under Sports), not a first-class product — Stake competes with Hula Na on vibe and liquidity theater, not on market mechanics. Strategically retreating from strict regimes (exited UK Mar 2025 after a Gambling Commission investigation) while pursuing local licenses (Mexico, Colombia C1751, Peru).
visualLanguage: Directly measured from archived stylesheets (Jul 3–4, 2026 captures): body canvas rgb(26,46,57) ≈ #1A2E39 dark desaturated slate-blue; raised cards/segments rgb(32,55,67) ≈ #203743; secondary buttons rgb(57,85,101) ≈ #395565; single saturated primary — "Register" CTA rgb(20,117,225) ≈ #1475E1 blue with white text; bright text #F7FAFC, muted blue-grey body text #B1BAD3, link tint #9FBED0. Consistent 8px corner radius on buttons/cards, fully-rounded (9999px) pill segmented controls for feed toggles ("Casino Bets"/"Sports Bets", "All Bets"/"High Rollers"). The chrome itself is restrained and flat — near-monochrome slate with one blue accent — and all the visual noise comes from game-tile art ("signature dark theme with bursts of colour," per their own casino copy). Casino lobby = dense horizontal carousels of portrait art tiles; sportsbook = tabular odds buttons in threes (1x2) with market counts. Ambient dynamism everywhere: live "N playing" counters on every tile, scrolling bet feeds with user/bet/multiplier/payout columns, promo banners with countdown timestamps. Celebration is carried by promo art and jackpot counters ("JAQKpot! Win up to $1M!", "$500,000 All in or Fold Jackpot") rather than confetti in the chrome.
typographyBrand: Directly measured font stack: "proxima-nova, ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif" — a licensed geometric-humanist sans used at 16px base, weight 400 for body and 600 for buttons, nav labels, and card titles; no serif or display face anywhere in the app chrome. Type does almost no expressive work — hierarchy is carried by color (bright vs muted blue-grey) and weight, keeping the UI quiet under loud game art. Brand voice is superlative-heavy: "unrivalled VIP experience," "unbeatable odds," "award winning support," "instantly withdrawable bonuses without any strings attached." Numbers are the real brand assets: dollar prize pools ($100,000 Daily Races, $75,000 Weekly Raffle), player counts, and wager totals are typeset as first-class UI content.
navigationDiscovery: Root split is a two-product toggle: Casino | Sports, each showing live occupancy ("Casino 50,066 / Sports 40,798" users online). A toggleable left sidebar groups: casino categories (Only on Stake, New Releases, Slots, Stake Originals, Live Casino, Game Shows, Burst Games, Enhanced RTP, Stake Poker, Bonus Buy, Blackjack, Baccarat, Roulette, Publishers) then platform links (Promotions, Challenges, Affiliate, VIP Club, Blog, Forum, Sponsorships, Responsible Gambling, Live Support). Sports sidebar leads with Live Events (count badge, e.g. "32"), Starting Soon, My Bets, then Top Sports (Soccer, Tennis, Baseball, Cricket, Basketball, F1, Horse Racing, CS2, Dota 2, LoL) and All Sports/All Esports/All Racing indexes. Discovery inside a page is horizontal carousels — Trending Games, Stake Originals, per-publisher rows, themed rows (World Cup) — each with View All + Load More, plus a search bar with filters. Logged-in personalization rows: "Continue Playing," "Games For You," "Saved Games," "My Bets." An odds-format switcher ("Odds: Decimal") and language selector sit in global nav. Promotions page has category tabs (All/Casino/Sport/Community/Poker/Esports). Very deep catalogue (6,000+ games) made navigable by aggressive categorization rather than search-first UX.
marketCardAnatomy: Two card grammars. Casino tile: portrait art, game title, publisher name, live "N playing" count (e.g. "Dice — Stake Originals — 2,575 playing"); region-locked tiles carry an inline "Not available in your region" label. Sports event card: time-to-start ("14h") or Live badge; a viewer/bettor count (e.g. "18,344"); team names; market label with settlement scope spelled out on the card — "1x2 (90' + stoppage time)"; three tappable odds buttons (e.g. 5.40 / 3.55 / 1.70); a "+127" chip for additional market count; and a crowd-consensus strip — "82% of 1x2 bets on Canada." "Top Picks" cards add total money signals: "$538,394 Wagered." Outright/futures cards (the prediction-market analog) are ranked outcome lists with decimal odds (World Cup Winner: France 4.00, Argentina 4.80 … + Load More). "Big Bets" feed rows show event, bet amount, market, selection, odds — including a "Suspended" state on the odds button. Promo cards are uniform: category tag, title, one-line hook, "Ends at" timestamp, single CTA ("Bet Now"/"Play Now"/"Read More").
tradeTicketClarity: Bet slip (per 2026 Covers/CryptoSlate reviews) pops out on the right, is collapsible, and supports singles/parlays/same-game multis with stake input → potential payout math shown before confirm; cashout appears as a button inside the slip for live positions; odds format is user-switchable (decimal/fractional/American). "Stake Shield" is an in-slip insurance feature unlocked at 3+ parlay legs. There is no explicit fee line anywhere — the sportsbook margin lives invisibly inside odds, and the compensating narrative is rakeback ("refunds you a percentage of each bet you place, whether it wins or loses"). Casino games invert this: house edge is documented per game (Dice: 1% edge / 99% RTP, payout multipliers 1.0102x–9900x shown in-game), every Originals game has a Fairness tab with per-round provably-fair verification, and demo mode is a one-flip "Real Play / Fun Play" toggle. Resolution rules for sports are pushed to footer docs ("Sports Rules," "Racing Rules") rather than surfaced on the card or slip — the only rule text at point of bet is the market label itself ("90' + stoppage time"). Net: excellent speed-to-bet and payout preview; poor cost transparency and rules-at-point-of-decision.
trustRiskSafety: Footer discloses operator identity precisely (Medium Rare N.V., reg 145353, Curaçao address, payment agents, support email) and links Gamblingtherapy.org. A dedicated "Stake Smart" hub (directly captured) offers: loss limits, wager limits, deposit limits (day/week/month), Break in Play (1 day/1 week/1 month), and self-exclusion (indefinite; minimum 6 months; reactivation only via formal review) — with a genuinely well-designed asymmetry: decreasing a limit is immediate, increasing/removing takes a 24-hour cooling-off. It also plainly teaches house edge, randomness, and independence of outcomes, and links GA, Gambling Therapy, NCPG, Gamtalk, BetBlocker/GamBlock. Weaknesses: crypto deposit limits use a "withholding balance" that auto-releases every day (a soft valve, not a hard stop); disputes/complaints route through support email/chat with "at our sole discretion" account-closure language; no on-card resolution rules; no visible vig. External record: exited UK Mar 2025 under Gambling Commission investigation; Missouri class action (Oct 2025) against Stake + Drake alleging deceptive "harmless gameplay" framing and that the tipping feature disguises wagering; FTM investigation into Curaçao licensing; Trustpilot ≈3.8–3.9 with a ~21% one-star cluster alleging post-win account restrictions, 20-day withdrawal waits, repeat-KYC document loops, and cancelled bonuses. Cookie banner is a single "Accept" with no decline option.
socialCommunity: Community is a retention engine, structurally load-bearing: (1) always-on public bet feeds on home/casino/sports pages — tables of Game/User/Time/Bet Amount/Multiplier/Payout with "All Bets" vs "High Rollers" pill tabs; (2) global chat with an hourly "Chat Rain" rainbot that drops bonus funds on active chatters (activity-gated), plus user-to-user tipping (the feature named in the class action); (3) Forum and Blog as first-class nav items, with forum-linked promos ("Streak Rush — Forum Challenge"); (4) Telegram channels including a VIP-gated one; (5) competitive social formats — $100,000 Daily Races (wager leaderboard every 24h), $75,000 Weekly Raffle, Challenges page, "Stake vs Eddie" ($50k/week vs a house personality); (6) crowd data on cards ("82% of 1x2 bets on Canada") and money leaderboards ("$538,394 Wagered"). Sponsorships (own nav item) extend community to UFC/Drake/F1-Kick parasocial reach — the same "win-oriented social strategy" critics say attracts minors.
mobileUsability: Deliberately PWA-first: no Android app at all, iOS "Stake: Real Money Casino" app only in select regions; everywhere else the official path is the mobile browser + "Add to Home Screen," which Stake documents as "downloading the app." Their copy frames this as HTML5/no-download convenience; the practical driver is app-store gambling restrictions and geo-fragmentation. Reviews (Goal.com Jul 2026, TheSpike 2026) describe the mobile web experience as fully featured — same wallet, bet slip, live streams, chat — with the collapsible sidebar becoming a drawer. Consequences worth noting: no store-review trust surface, no OS-level self-exclusion hooks, updates ship instantly without review, and deep links stay in-browser. For a crypto-native, outside-app-store product like ours, this is the reference implementation that a PWA-only distribution strategy can reach massive scale — but it also shows the cost: installability education has to live in-product ("download the app" guides in blog/FAQ).
learnFrom: Two-product root nav with live occupancy counts (Casino 50,066 / Sports 40,798) — orientation plus ambient liquidity proof in one control; a prediction-market analog is live trader/open-interest counts per category tab.
Persistent public activity feed (User/Time/Amount/Multiplier/Payout with All vs High Rollers tabs) as a liquidity heartbeat — for markets, a recent-trades tape makes thin markets legible and honest.
Per-card live counters ('2,575 playing', '18,344' watching, '$538,394 Wagered') — popularity as data on the card, not a separate leaderboard page.

Settlement scope written on the card itself ('1x2 (90\' + stoppage time)') — the one place Stake puts a resolution rule at point of decision; generalize this: every market card should carry its resolution criterion inline.
Odds-format toggle (Decimal/Fractional/American) persisted in global nav — respect heterogeneous mental models; for us: probability % vs price vs payout toggle.

Provably-fair Fairness tab per game with per-round verification — the UX pattern (verify this exact outcome, right here, after the fact) maps directly to on-chain resolution proofs and beats a buried 'audits' page.
Asymmetric safety cooldowns: lowering a limit is instant, raising one takes 24h — copy this exact mechanic for deposit/loss limits.
One-flip 'Real Play / Fun Play' demo toggle on every game — zero-risk onboarding without a separate sandbox build; a paper-trading toggle per market is the analog.
PWA-first mobile with in-product add-to-homescreen education — proven at 100M-user scale for a crypto product locked out of app stores.
Quiet chrome, loud content: near-monochrome slate UI (#1A2E39/#203743, one blue #1475E1, one typeface at two weights) lets data and market art carry all color — dense screens stay calm.
Right-side pop-out, collapsible ticket with payout preview and in-slip cashout — browse-to-position in one gesture, position management in the same surface.
SSR text shell under the SPA (whole catalog and footer render serverside) — fast first paint, SEO, and graceful degradation.
avoid: Wager-race economies: $100,000 Daily Races, $75,000 Weekly Raffle, $150,000 Wheel Wars — leaderboards that pay for volume convert engagement into churn-and-burn wagering; never rank users by amount staked.

The VIP ladder as core loyalty: Bronze $10k → Diamond $25M wager thresholds, level-up bonuses, 'money back on losses every time you level up', and a 'dedicated VIP host' — a losses-as-status machine; the human host assigned at ~$2.5M wagered is a retention agent for the heaviest losers.
Rakeback framing that converts house edge into a reward ('refunds a percentage of each bet, win or lose') — it reframes cost as generosity while hiding the actual fee; show fees as fees.
Countdown urgency stitched into every promo card ('Ends at 12:59 PM', 'Halftime Rush — be quick!') — scarcity pressure at point of purchase.

Copy/terms gap: 'bonuses without any strings attached' marketing alongside a documented complaint cluster of cancelled bonuses, post-win account restrictions and repeat-KYC withdrawal loops — the single biggest trust destroyer in their Trustpilot record.

Chat Rain + tipping: hourly bot drops gated on chat activity, and user-to-user transfers that a class action alleges disguise wagering as social interaction — don't blend money movement into chat mechanics.
High-roller voyeurism ('High Rollers' feed tab, 'Big Bets' $18,000 rows) — normalizes oversized positions and models risky behavior as aspirational.

Crowd-percentage strips used as bet prompts ('82% of bets on Canada' next to a tappable odds button) — fine as information, manipulative as a nudge adjacent to the buy button; if shown, separate it from the action.
Invisible pricing: no vig/fee line anywhere in the slip; margin buried in odds while resolution rules hide in footer docs ('Sports Rules') — surface both at the ticket.

Soft safety valves: crypto deposit-limit 'withholding balance' that re-releases funds daily, support-email-only dispute path, and 'at our sole discretion' closure clauses — safety tools must be hard stops with an auditable dispute process.
Single-button 'Accept' cookie banner with no decline — a small tell that compounds the dark-pattern picture.
Superlative claim inflation ('World's Largest', 'unbeatable odds', 'award winning support') — unverifiable claims that regulators and journalists (FTM, Harvard JSEL) now quote back as evidence.

evidenceNotes: DIRECT EVIDENCE: Live stake.com blocked both WebFetch (HTTP 403) and browser access (Cloudflare bot-verification interstitial, which I did not attempt to bypass). All on-site claims therefore come from Internet Archive Wayback captures dated Jul 3–4 2026 (homepage, /casino/home, /sports/home, /vip-club, /promotions, /responsible-gambling/stake-smart) — these delivered the full server-rendered DOM text, so nav structure, card contents, promo copy, VIP tiers, RG tool descriptions, footer/license text, and the '82% of bets'/'$ Wagered'/'N playing' data patterns are directly observed, as are visual tokens extracted via computed CSS on the archived pages (body #1A2E39, cards #203743, CTA #1475E1, text #F7FAFC/#B1BAD3, proxima-nova, 8px radii, pill tabs). Client-side hydration never completed in the archive, so I could NOT visually render pages — no screenshot-level claims (layout spacing, animations, hover states) are made. Archive crawler geo caused 'Not available in your region' labels on live-casino tiles; I report the label pattern, not regional availability. INFERENCE: bet-slip pop-out behavior, cashout placement, mobile drawer behavior, Chat Rain mechanics, iOS-app regionality, Trustpilot themes, and rakeback percentages come from 2025–2026 secondary reviews/news (cited) — consistent across multiple sources but not observed first-hand; the 'quiet chrome / loud content' and SSR-performance points are inferences from the captured DOM/CSS. VIP tier thresholds are triple-sourced (archived VIP page + archived casino-lobby table + reviews) — high confidence. ASSUMPTION (flagged, low weight): green/red odds-movement coloring and confetti-style win animations are industry-standard and widely described for Stake Originals, but I did not verify them; I kept them out of the scorecard. Trustpilot score varies 3.8–3.9 by snapshot; treat as approximate. The lawsuit and UK-exit characterizations follow the cited reporting; allegations in the Missouri class action are allegations, not findings.
